title: Two Laredo Men Sentenced to Federal Prison in Card-Skimming Scheme That Compromised 1,500 Cards
excerpt: Two Cuban nationals living in Laredo were sentenced to federal prison for a card-fraud scheme that compromised more than 1,500 credit and debit card numbers, including a federal agent's government travel card, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.
content:
Two Cuban nationals living in Laredo were sentenced to federal prison for a credit card fraud scheme that compromised more than 1,500 credit and debit card numbers, including a federal agent's government travel card, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

Visiting U.S. District Judge Ivan L.R. Lemelle sentenced Liover Leon-Hernandez, 33, to 46 months in prison and Orlandi Castillo Leon, 35, to 37 months, federal prosecutors said. Both men pleaded guilty earlier this year to possessing 15 or more counterfeit or unauthorized access devices with intent to defraud and to using other people's identifying information without lawful authority. Leon pleaded guilty April 8 and Leon-Hernandez on May 6.

The investigation began March 31, 2025, when a U.S. Customs and Border Protection special agent reported fraudulent charges on his government travel card at a Laredo grocery store, according to prosecutors. Store video showed the men using seven card accounts belonging to other people to buy gift cards and merchandise, and investigators traced several victims to payments at the same location, where they found a skimming device in a gas pump.

When authorities searched the men's shared home on July 16, 2025, Leon-Hernandez attempted to swallow a thumb drive containing 1,530 stolen card numbers, prosecutors said.

Leon-Hernandez is a lawful permanent resident and Leon is an asylum seeker, according to prosecutors, and both are expected to face removal proceedings after serving their sentences. Both men remain in custody pending transfer to a federal prison.

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas, Nov. 19, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 19, 2026.
